sanskrit: pātito bhuvi bhīmas tu kīcakena balīyasā utpapātātha vegena daṇḍāhata ivoragaḥ
english: Though knocked to the ground by the mighty Kīcaka, Bhīma leapt up again with speed, like a serpent struck by a rod.

sanskrit: spardhayā ca balonmattau tāv ubhau sūtapāṇḍavau niśīthe paryakarṣetāṃ balinau niśi nirjane
english: Drunk on their own strength and rival pride, that pair—the charioteer's son and the Pāṇḍava—grappled and dragged each other at midnight in the deserted darkness.

sanskrit: tatas tad bhavanaśreṣṭhaṃ prākampata muhur muhuḥ balavac cāpi saṃkruddhāv anyonyaṃ tāv agarjatām
english: That finest of halls trembled again and again, and the two mighty men, blazing with fury, roared at each other.

sanskrit: talābhyāṃ tu sa bhīmena vakṣasy abhihato balī kīcako roṣasaṃtaptaḥ padān na calitaḥ padam
english: Though struck on the chest by Bhīma's open palms, the mighty Kīcaka, burning with rage, did not give a single step of ground.

sanskrit: muhūrtaṃ tu sa taṃ vegaṃ sahitvā bhuvi duḥsaham balād ahīyata tadā sūto bhīmabalārditaḥ
english: But after bearing for a moment that assault—hard to endure on earth—the charioteer, tormented by Bhīma's power, at last began to falter.

sanskrit: taṃ hīyamānaṃ vijñāya bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ vakṣasy ānīya vegena mamanthainaṃ vicetasam
english: Perceiving him flagging, the great-powered Bhīmasena swiftly seized him against his chest and churned him until he lost his senses.

sanskrit: krodhāviṣṭo viniḥśvasya punaś cainaṃ vṛkodaraḥ jagrāha jayatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ keśeṣv eva tadā bhṛśam
english: Possessed by fury, Vṛkodara—best among the victorious—exhaled a hot breath and seized him violently by the hair.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā kīcakaṃ bhīmo virurāva mahābalaḥ śārdūlaḥ piśitākāṅkṣī gṛhītveva mahāmṛgam
english: Gripping Kīcaka, the mighty Bhīma let out a great roar, like a tiger that craves flesh having seized a great quarry.

sanskrit: tasya pādau ca pāṇī ca śiro grīvāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ kāye praveśayām āsa paśor iva pinākadhṛk
english: His feet, his hands, his head, his neck—all of them Bhīma thrust entirely into his body, as Śiva the bearer of the Pināka bow does to a beast.

sanskrit: taṃ saṃmathitasarvāṅgaṃ māṃsapiṇḍopamaṃ kṛtam kṛṣṇāyai darśayām āsa bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: Having reduced him—all his limbs crushed—to a mere lump of flesh, the mighty Bhīmasena showed him to Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: uvāca ca mahātejā draupadīṃ pāṇḍunandanaḥ paśyainam ehi pāñcāli kāmuko 'yaṃ yathā kṛtaḥ
english: And the blazing son of Pāṇḍu said to Draupadī: 'Come and see, Pāñcālī, what has been made of this lustful one.'

sanskrit: tathā sa kīcakaṃ hatvā gatvā roṣasya vai śamam āmantrya draupadīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kṣipram āyān mahānasam
english: Having thus slain Kīcaka and letting his rage subside, he took leave of Kṛṣṇā Draupadī and quickly returned to the royal kitchen.

sanskrit: kīcakaṃ ghātayitvā tu draupadī yoṣitāṃ varā prahṛṣṭā gatasaṃtāpā sabhāpālān uvāca ha
english: And Draupadī, best among women, having seen Kīcaka slain, was filled with joy, her anguish gone, and she spoke to the guards of the hall.

sanskrit: kīcako 'yaṃ hataḥ śete gandharvaiḥ patibhir mama parastrīkāmasaṃmattaḥ samāgacchata paśyata
english: 'This Kīcaka lies slain—by my gandharva husbands—he who was maddened by lust for another man's wife. Come together and see.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasyā nartanāgārarakṣiṇaḥ sahasaiva samājagmur ādāyolkāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Hearing her words, the guards of the dance hall came rushing together at once, carrying torches by the thousands.

sanskrit: tato gatvātha tad veśma kīcakaṃ vinipātitam gatāsuṃ dadṛśur bhūmau rudhireṇa samukṣitam
english: Going to that chamber, they saw Kīcaka flung down—lifeless, drenched in blood upon the ground.

sanskrit: kvāsya grīvā kva caraṇau kva pāṇī kva śiras tathā iti sma taṃ parīkṣante gandharveṇa hataṃ tadā
english: "Where is his neck? Where his feet? Where his hands? Where his head?"—thus they examined him, slain by the gandharva.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmin kāle samāgamya sarve tatrāsya bāndhavāḥ ruruduḥ kīcakaṃ dṛṣṭvā parivārya samantataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: At that time all his kinsmen gathered there; surrounding Kīcaka on all sides, they wept at the sight of him.

sanskrit: sarve saṃhṛṣṭaromāṇaḥ saṃtrastāḥ prekṣya kīcakam tathā sarvāṅgasaṃbhugnaṃ kūrmaṃ sthala ivoddhṛtam
english: Their hair standing on end, all of them terrified, they beheld Kīcaka with every limb crushed inward, like a tortoise dragged out onto dry land.

sanskrit: pothitaṃ bhīmasenena tam indreṇeva dānavam saṃskārayitum icchanto bahir netuṃ pracakramuḥ
english: Pounded by Bhīmasena as Indra pounds a demon, they resolved to perform his last rites and began carrying him outside.

sanskrit: dadṛśus te tataḥ kṛṣṇāṃ sūtaputrāḥ samāgatāḥ adūrād anavadyāṅgīṃ stambham āliṅgya tiṣṭhatīm
english: Then those assembled charioteer-sons caught sight of Kṛṣṇā not far away—her limbs flawless—standing there clinging to a pillar.

sanskrit: samaveteṣu sūteṣu tān uvācopakīcakaḥ hanyatāṃ śīghram asatī yatkṛte kīcako hataḥ
english: When the charioteer-sons had assembled, the leader of the Upakīcakas spoke to them: 'Let this unchaste woman be killed at once—she for whose sake Kīcaka was slain.'

sanskrit: atha vā neha hantavyā dahyatāṃ kāminā saha mṛtasyāpi priyaṃ kāryaṃ sūtaputrasya sarvathā
english: 'Or rather, she should not be killed here—let her be burned together with her lover. Even in death, what is dear to the charioteer's son must be done in every way.'

sanskrit: tato virāṭam ūcus te kīcako 'syāḥ kṛte hataḥ sahādyānena dahyeta tadanujñātum arhasi
english: Then they went to Virāṭa and said: 'Kīcaka was slain on account of this woman; she should be burned with him today—please grant your permission.'

sanskrit: parākramaṃ tu sūtānāṃ matvā rājānvamodata sairandhryāḥ sūtaputreṇa saha dāhaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Considering the valor of the charioteer-clan, O lord of the people, the king gave his consent that the Sairandhrī be burned together with the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: tāṃ samāsādya vitrastāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kamalalocanām momuhyamānāṃ te tatra jagṛhuḥ kīcakā bhṛśam
english: Approaching the trembling, lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇā as she was fainting, the Kīcakas there seized her violently.

sanskrit: tatas tu tāṃ samāropya nibadhya ca sumadhyamām jagmur udyamya te sarve śmaśānam abhitas tadā
english: They lifted her up, bound the slender-waisted woman, and all of them set out, carrying her toward the cremation ground.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇā tu sā rājan sūtaputrair aninditā prākrośan nātham icchantī kṛṣṇā nāthavatī satī
english: As she was being dragged away, O king, by the charioteer-sons, blameless Kṛṣṇā—a true wife longing for her protector—cried out aloud.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca jayo jayanto vijayo jayatseno jayadbalaḥ te me vācaṃ vijānantu sūtaputrā nayanti mām
english: Draupadī cried: 'Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena, Jayadbala—let them hear my words: the charioteer-sons are taking me away!'

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ jyātalanirghoṣo visphūrjitam ivāśaneḥ vyaśrūyata mahāyuddhe bhīmaghoṣas tarasvinām
english: 'Those whose bowstring-twang sounds in great battle like the crash of a thunderbolt—the fierce, dreadful roar of those swift ones—'

sanskrit: rathaghoṣaś ca balavān gandharvāṇāṃ yaśasvinām te me vācaṃ vijānantu sūtaputrā nayanti mām
english: '—and the mighty chariot-thunder of those glorious gandharvas—let them hear my words: the charioteer-sons are taking me away!'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasyās tāḥ kṛpaṇā vācaḥ kṛṣṇāyāḥ paridevitāḥ śrutvaivābhyapatad bhīmaḥ śayanād avicārayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those pitiful, lamenting words of Kṛṣṇā, Bhīma leapt from his bed without a moment's hesitation.

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca ahaṃ śṛṇomi te vācaṃ tvayā sairandhri bhāṣitām tasmāt te sūtaputrebhyo na bhayaṃ bhīru vidyate
english: Bhīmasena said: 'I hear the words you have spoken, Sairandhrī. Therefore, timid one, you need have no fear from the charioteer-sons.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā sa mahābāhur vijajṛmbhe jighāṃsayā tataḥ sa vyāyataṃ kṛtvā veṣaṃ viparivartya ca advāreṇābhyavaskandya nirjagāma bahis tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having said this, the mighty-armed one stretched himself with the desire to kill; then, adjusting his disguise and wrapping it around, he leapt out through a side passage and issued forth.

sanskrit: sa bhīmasenaḥ prākārād ārujya tarasā drumam śmaśānābhimukhaḥ prāyād yatra te kīcakā gatāḥ
english: Bhīmasena swiftly tore a tree from the rampart wall and set off toward the cremation ground, where the Kīcakas had gone.

sanskrit: sa taṃ vṛkṣaṃ daśavyāmaṃ saskandhaviṭapaṃ balī pragṛhyābhyadravat sūtān daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: Grasping that tree—ten fathoms long, with its trunk and branches intact—the mighty one charged at the charioteers like Yama with his staff.

sanskrit: ūruvegena tasyātha nyagrodhāśvatthakiṃśukāḥ bhūmau nipatitā vṛkṣāḥ saṃghaśas tatra śerate
english: From the force of his thighs as he ran, the nyagrodha, aśvattha, and kiṃśuka trees fell to the ground and lay there in heaps.

sanskrit: taṃ siṃham iva saṃkruddhaṃ dṛṣṭvā gandharvam āgatam vitresuḥ sarvataḥ sūtā viṣādabhayakampitāḥ
english: Seeing the gandharva arrive like a lion blazing with fury, the charioteers were terrified on all sides, trembling with dread and despair.

sanskrit: tam antakam ivāyāntaṃ gandharvaṃ prekṣya te tadā didhakṣantas tadā jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ hy upakīcakāḥ parasparam athocus te viṣādabhayakampitāḥ
english: Seeing that gandharva approaching like Death himself, the Upakīcakas—who had been about to burn their eldest brother—said to one another, trembling with fear and despair:

sanskrit: gandharvo balavān eti kruddha udyamya pādapam sairandhrī mucyatāṃ śīghraṃ mahan no bhayam āgatam
english: 'A mighty gandharva comes in rage, raising up a tree! Release the Sairandhrī at once—great danger has come upon us!'

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvā tam āviddhaṃ bhīmasenena pādapam vimucya draupadīṃ tatra prādravan nagaraṃ prati
english: Seeing the tree whirled by Bhīmasena, they released Draupadī on the spot and fled toward the city.

sanskrit: dravatas tāṃs tu saṃprekṣya sa vajrī dānavān iva śataṃ pañcādhikaṃ bhīmaḥ prāhiṇod yamasādanam
english: Watching them flee as Indra watches fleeing demons, Bhīma dispatched one hundred and five of them to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tata āśvāsayat kṛṣṇāṃ pravimucya viśāṃ pate uvāca ca mahābāhuḥ pāñcālīṃ tatra draupadīm aśrupūrṇamukhīṃ dīnāṃ durdharṣaḥ sa vṛkodaraḥ
english: Then, O lord of the people, he set her free and comforted Kṛṣṇā; the invincible Vṛkodara, the mighty-armed one, spoke there to the Pāñcālī Draupadī, whose face was filled with tears and who was wretched.

sanskrit: evaṃ te bhīru vadhyante ye tvāṃ kliśyanty anāgasam praihi tvaṃ nagaraṃ kṛṣṇe na bhayaṃ vidyate tava anyenāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi virāṭasya mahānasam
english: 'Thus, timid one, are those slain who torment you though you are innocent. Go to the city, Kṛṣṇā—you have nothing to fear. I shall go back by a different way to Virāṭa's kitchen.'

sanskrit: pañcādhikaṃ śataṃ tac ca nihataṃ tatra bhārata mahāvanam iva chinnaṃ śiśye vigalitadrumam
english: And those one hundred and five lay slain there, O Bhārata, like a great forest felled, its trees scattered about.

sanskrit: evaṃ te nihatā rājañ śataṃ pañca ca kīcakāḥ sa ca senāpatiḥ pūrvam ity etat sūtaṣaṭśatam
english: Thus, O king, those one hundred and five Kīcakas were slain, along with the general who was killed before—making a total of six hundred charioteers.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryaṃ narā nāryaś ca saṃgatāḥ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatvā nocuḥ kiṃ cana bhārata
english: Seeing that great wonder, the men and women who had gathered fell into the utmost amazement and said not a single word, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te dṛṣṭvā nihatān sūtān rājñe gatvā nyavedayan gandharvair nihatā rājan sūtaputrāḥ paraḥśatāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those who had seen the charioteers slain went and reported to the king: 'O king, more than a hundred charioteer-sons have been killed by the gandharvas.'

sanskrit: yathā vajreṇa vai dīrṇaṃ parvatasya mahac chiraḥ vinikīrṇaṃ pradṛśyeta tathā sūtā mahītale
english: 'As the great summit of a mountain shattered by the thunderbolt might be seen scattered about, so lay the charioteers on the earth.'

sanskrit: sairandhrī ca vimuktāsau punar āyāti te gṛham sarvaṃ saṃśayitaṃ rājan nagaraṃ te bhaviṣyati
english: 'The Sairandhrī has been released and is coming back to your house again. O king, your entire city will be thrown into doubt and danger.'

sanskrit: tathārūpā hi sairandhrī gandharvāś ca mahābalāḥ puṃsām iṣṭaś ca viṣayo maithunāya na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'For the Sairandhrī is of such a beauty, and the gandharvas are of such great power, and the subject of desire between men is without doubt agreeable for union.'

sanskrit: yathā sairandhriveṣeṇa na te rājann idaṃ puram vināśam eti vai kṣipraṃ tathā nītir vidhīyatām
english: 'Therefore, O king, such a policy must be devised that your city does not quickly come to ruin through keeping the Sairandhrī here.'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ abravīt kriyatām eṣāṃ sūtānāṃ paramakriyā
english: Hearing their words, Virāṭa, lord of the army, said: 'Let the final rites of these charioteers be performed.'

sanskrit: ekasminn eva te sarve susamiddhe hutāśane dahyantāṃ kīcakāḥ śīghraṃ ratnair gandhaiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: 'Let all the Kīcakas be burned quickly together in a single well-kindled fire, with jewels and fragrances of every kind.'

sanskrit: sudeṣṇāṃ cābravīd rājā mahiṣīṃ jātasādhvasaḥ sairandhrīm āgatāṃ brūyā mamaiva vacanād idam
english: The king, seized with fear, also said to his queen Sudeṣṇā: 'When the Sairandhrī arrives, tell her this on my behalf:'

sanskrit: gaccha sairandhri bhadraṃ te yathākāmaṃ carābale bibheti rājā suśroṇi gandharvebhyaḥ parābhavāt
english: '"Go, Sairandhrī, be well—go wherever you wish, dear girl. The king, O fine-hipped one, fears defeat at the hands of the gandharvas."'

sanskrit: na hi tām utsahe vaktuṃ svayaṃ gandharvarakṣitām striyas tv adoṣās tāṃ vaktum atas tvāṃ prabravīmy aham
english: 'I do not dare to speak to her myself—she who is protected by gandharvas. But women are without fault in speaking to her, and so I charge you to tell her.'

sanskrit: atha muktā bhayāt kṛṣṇā sūtaputrān nirasya ca mokṣitā bhīmasenena jagāma nagaraṃ prati
english: Then Kṛṣṇā, freed from fear, the charioteer-sons driven off, having been rescued by Bhīmasena, made her way toward the city.

sanskrit: trāsiteva mṛgī bālā śārdūlena manasvinī gātrāṇi vāsasī caiva prakṣālya salilena sā
english: Like a young doe frightened by a tiger, the high-minded one washed her limbs and garments with water.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣā rājan prādravanta diśo daśa gandharvāṇāṃ bhayatrastāḥ ke cid dṛṣṭīr nyamīlayan
english: Seeing her, O king, men fled in all ten directions, terrified of the gandharvas; some shut their eyes tight.

sanskrit: tato mahānasadvāri bhīmasenam avasthitam dadarśa rājan pāñcālī yathā mattaṃ mahādvipam
english: Then, O king, the Pāñcālī saw Bhīmasena standing at the kitchen door—like a mighty elephant in rut.

sanskrit: taṃ vismayantī śanakaiḥ saṃjñābhir idam abravīt gandharvarājāya namo yenāsmi parimocitā
english: Marveling at him, she approached slowly and said with a gesture: 'Homage to the king of the gandharvas, by whom I have been freed.'

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca ye yasyā vicarantīha puruṣā vaśavartinaḥ tasyās te vacanaṃ śrutvā anṛṇā vicaranty uta
english: Bhīmasena said: 'Those men who move about here as her obedient servants—having heard her word, they move about free of debt.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sā nartanāgāre dhanaṃjayam apaśyata rājñaḥ kanyā virāṭasya nartayānaṃ mahābhujam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then she saw in the dance hall Dhanaṃjaya—the great-armed one—teaching the dance to the daughters of king Virāṭa.

sanskrit: tatas tā nartanāgārād viniṣkramya sahārjunāḥ kanyā dadṛśur āyāntīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kliṣṭām anāgasam
english: Then the girls, coming out of the dance hall together with Arjuna, saw Kṛṣṇā approaching—afflicted but blameless.

sanskrit: kanyā ūcuḥ diṣṭyā sairandhri muktāsi diṣṭyāsi punarāgatā diṣṭyā vinihatāḥ sūtā ye tvāṃ kliśyanty anāgasam
english: The girls said: 'By good fortune, Sairandhrī, you are freed! By good fortune you have come back! By good fortune the charioteers who tormented you though innocent are slain!'

sanskrit: bṛhannaḍovāca kathaṃ sairandhri muktāsi kathaṃ pāpāś ca te hatāḥ icchāmi vai tava śrotuṃ sarvam eva yathātatham
english: Bṛhannaḍā said: 'How were you freed, Sairandhrī? And how were those sinners killed? I wish to hear everything from you, exactly as it happened.'

sanskrit: sairandhry uvāca bṛhannaḍe kiṃ nu tava sairandhryā kāryam adya vai yā tvaṃ vasasi kalyāṇi sadā kanyāpure sukham
english: The Sairandhrī said: 'What business do you have today with the Sairandhrī, Bṛhannaḍā? You who always dwell in comfort, dear one, in the girls' quarters?'

sanskrit: na hi duḥkhaṃ samāpnoṣi sairandhrī yad upāśnute tena māṃ duḥkhitām evaṃ pṛcchase prahasann iva
english: 'You do not suffer the pain that the Sairandhrī endures, and yet you question me in my grief as if laughing.'

sanskrit: bṛhannaḍovāca bṛhannaḍāpi kalyāṇi duḥkham āpnoty anuttamam tiryagyonigatā bāle na cainām avabudhyase
english: Bṛhannaḍā said: 'Even Bṛhannaḍā, dear lady, suffers the most extreme grief—born into an in-between existence, young woman—yet you do not understand her.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sahaiva kanyābhir draupadī rājaveśma tat praviveśa sudeṣṇāyāḥ samīpam apalāyinī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Draupadī, unflinching, entered that royal palace together with the girls, and came before Sudeṣṇā.

sanskrit: tām abravīd rājaputrī virāṭavacanād idam sairandhri gamyatāṃ śīghraṃ yatra kāmayase gatim
english: The princess said to her the words of Virāṭa: 'Sairandhrī, go quickly wherever you wish to go.'

sanskrit: rājā bibheti bhadraṃ te gandharvebhyaḥ parābhavāt tvaṃ cāpi taruṇī subhru rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi
english: 'The king, be assured, fears defeat at the hands of the gandharvas, and you too are young, O fine-browed one, unmatched in beauty upon the earth.'

sanskrit: sairandhry uvāca trayodaśāhamātraṃ me rājā kṣamatu bhāmini kṛtakṛtyā bhaviṣyanti gandharvās te na saṃśayaḥ
english: The Sairandhrī said: 'Let the king grant me merely thirteen days, dear lady; the gandharvas will have accomplished their purpose, without doubt.'

sanskrit: tato māṃ te 'paneṣyanti kariṣyanti ca te priyam dhruvaṃ ca śreyasā rājā yokṣyate saha bāndhavaiḥ
english: 'Then they will take me away and do what is pleasing; and the king will certainly be joined with prosperity together with his kinsmen.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kīcakasya tu ghātena sānujasya viśāṃ pate atyāhitaṃ cintayitvā vyasmayanta pṛthagjanāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: O lord of the people, at the slaying of Kīcaka together with his younger brothers, the common people reflected on that great calamity and were filled with wonder.

sanskrit: tasmin pure janapade saṃjalpo 'bhūc ca sarvaśaḥ śauryād dhi vallabho rājño mahāsattvaś ca kīcakaḥ
english: Throughout that city and countryside, talk spread on every side: 'By his valor Kīcaka was the king's favorite and a man of great spirit—'

sanskrit: āsīt prahartā ca nṛṇāṃ dārāmarśī ca durmatiḥ sa hataḥ khalu pāpātmā gandharvair duṣṭapūruṣaḥ
english: '—he was a striker of men, an ill-minded violator of others' wives; that evil-souled, wicked man has been slain by the gandharvas, as was fitting.'

sanskrit: ity ajalpan mahārāja parānīkaviśātanam deśe deśe manuṣyāś ca kīcakaṃ duṣpradharṣaṇam
english: Thus people in every region spoke, O great king, destroyer of enemy armies, of Kīcaka who had been so hard to assail.

sanskrit: atha vai dhārtarāṣṭreṇa prayuktā ye bahiścarāḥ mṛgayitvā bahūn grāmān rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca
english: Now those spies sent out by the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having searched through many villages, kingdoms, and cities—
